column2: Retain David's Hebron-born sons, Amnon firstborn by Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Daniel second by Abigail the Carmelite. Daniel is the selected name and is not replaced by another account's name.
Retain third Absalom with Mocha, Tholmai and Gedsour, and fourth Adonijah by Aggith. Both the maternal and royal-grandfather relationships remain explicit.
Retain fifth Saphatias by Abital and sixth Jethraam by his wife Agla. The explicit wife designation stays with the final maternal phrase rather than being generalized across all mothers.
Retain six Hebron-born sons, seven years and six months there and thirty-three years in Jerusalem. The reign totals remain as stated without chronological recalculation.
Retain Samaa, Sobab, Nathan and Solomon, four by Bersabee daughter of Amiel. The selected maternal patronymic and birth order are not harmonized to another account.
Retain Ibaar, Elisama and Eliphalet beginning the next list. Names repeated in verse 8 are not deleted from this first occurrence.
Retain Nage, Naphag and Janoue as the middle three of the nine-name list. No source-specific spelling is silently replaced by a familiar Samuel form.
Retain the second Elisama and Eliphalet, Eliada between them and the explicit total nine. The repetition is part of the selected enumeration, not an automated duplicate to remove.
Retain all these sons, the exception for concubines' sons and Themar as their sister. The excluded sons are not assumed to be included in the preceding numeric totals.
Retain Solomon's sons heading followed by Rehoboam and the successive his son links through Abia, Asa and Jehoshaphat. The nested descent is not flattened into four immediate sons of Solomon.
Retain Joram, Ahaziah and Joash, each his son. Repeated relationship phrases keep the chain audible.
Retain Amasias, Azariah and Joathan in the son succession. Joathan is not silently standardized to Jotham in this selected record.
Retain Ahaz, Hezekiah and Manasseh, each linked by his son. The succession is genealogical and adds no reign lengths here.
Retain Amon and Josiah and their repeated son relation, closing the royal chain. The next verse begins Josiah's multiple sons as a new group.
Retain Joanan firstborn, Joakim second, Sedekias third and Salloum fourth. This ordering is not rearranged to fit accession chronology.
Retain Joakim's sons heading and Jechonias his son, Sedekias his son. The repeated possessive permits a chain or grouped relation in English and is not silently converted to brothers.
column3: Does the second his son refer to Jechonias or resume Joakim as father?

column2: Retain Jechonia-asir as the inherited joined form and Salathiel his son. The publisher's joined presentation is recorded without claiming that asir has been resolved as a second personal name or a captivity epithet.
column3: Should asir be translated as a descriptive term, treated as a separate name or retained with Jechonia after lexical and textual review?

column2: Retain Melchiram, Phadaias, Sanesar, Jekemia, Osamo and Denethi continuing the list. No new father heading is inserted to resolve the preceding construction.
Retain Salathiel's sons Zerubbabel and Semei, followed by Zerubbabel's Mosollamos, Ananias and their sister Salomith. The selected Salathiel is not replaced by Phadaias from another witness.
Retain Asoube, Ool, Barachias, Asadias and Asobaesd and the explicit five. Their attachment continues the preceding family list without deleting its named sister.
Retain Ananias's sons heading and the chain from Phalletia through Isaiah, Raphaia, Orna, Abdia and Sechenia, each with his son. The selected singular links are not turned into plural clan headings.
Retain Sechenia's singular son Samaia and Samaia's five named sons followed by the stated six. The discrepancy remains; no sixth name is invented and Samaia is not silently counted as his own son.
column3: Does the six include the preceding generation or reflect another textual enumeration? Apparatus review is not yet supplied.

column2: Retain Noadia's Elithenan, Hezekiah and Ezrikam and total three. The selected father is not changed to a name from another genealogy.
Retain Elithenan's seven named sons and explicit total seven. The ordered list closes with Anani without an added generational continuation.
Retain Judah's Phares, Arson, Charmi, Or and Soubal, with the list continuing into verse 2. The sons heading is not made an assertion that every listed figure is an immediate child.
Retain Raia his son, then Soubal as the explicit begetting subject of Jeth and Jeth's Achimi and Laad. The selected subject Soubal is not changed to Raia to smooth the genealogy.
Retain Aitam's sons Jezrael, Ragma and Jabas and sister Eselebbōn. The inherited macron in the name remains pending systematic name-authority work.
Retain Phanouel/Gedor, Azer/Osan and Or as Ephratha's firstborn, Bethlehem's father. The placement of the final father phrase is provisionally inherited rather than a resolved settlement genealogy.
column3: Does Bethlehem's father attach to Or or another antecedent within the genitive sequence?

column2: Retain Saour as Thekoe's father and his two wives Aoda and Thoada. These selected names are not replaced by the differently formed names in another witness.
Retain Aoda as the mother of Ochazam, Hephad, Thaiman and Astheran and the repeated all these were Aoda's sons. The maternal name is not swapped to the second wife to harmonize the family sequence.
Retain Thoada's Sareth, Saar and Ethnan. The three-name list remains distinct from Aoda's four.

Retain Kos begetting Enob and Sabeba and the difficult generations-of-the-brother-of-Rechab clause. The inherited comma attaches an incomplete nominal continuation; it does not establish a newly understood family relation.
column3: Should the second clause be punctuated as a separate fragment, and how does brother of Rechab son of Jarim attach?

column2: Retain Igabes's greater renown than his brethren and the mother's naming explanation as gabes. The opaque expression is not translated as pain solely from another language's wordplay.
column3: What sense does the selected gabes expression convey, and how should the source's naming relation be explained without inventing an English etymology?

column2: Retain direct divine Thou/Thy, emphatic blessing within an if-clause, expanded borders, divine hand and knowledge so that he is not humbled. The selected knowledge/humbling construction is not replaced by a familiar evil/pain petition. All in God's response is explicit.
column3: How does the future knowledge clause connect to the initial condition, and is the non-humbling infinitive purpose or result?

column2: Retain Caleb as Ascha's father, begetting Machir, who is Assathon's father. No parallel name substitution or additional clan relation is introduced.
Retain Assathon's Bathrephan, Phessee and Thana, the city of Naas, brother of Eselon the Kenazite and men of Repha. The long father/city/brother sequence stays provisional.
column3: Which antecedent is Eselon's brother, and does the city-of-Naas phrase identify a settlement or compound name?

column2: Retain Kenaz's Othniel and Saraia and Othniel's plural sons heading with Athath alone. No absent second son is restored from another tradition.
Retain Manathi begetting Gophera, Saraia begetting Joab and Ageaddair followed by the craftsmen explanation. The place-like name is not silently translated as a craft valley without lexical evidence.
Retain Caleb son of Jephonne, his three sons Hera, Ala and Noom, and Ala's Kenaz. This explicitly identified Caleb is not automatically merged with every earlier Caleb branch.
Retain singular his son followed by Geseel, Ameachi, Zapha, Zaira and Eserael. The number and missing explicit new heading remain unresolved rather than changing son to sons.
column3: Does his son apply only to Geseel, with the remaining names forming another implicit list?

column2: Retain Esri's four sons and Jether explicitly begetting Maron, Semai and Mareth, Esthemon's father. The selected Jether subject is not replaced by a female pronoun or supplied spouse.

Retain his wife identified parenthetically as Adia, three sons with father-of-place relations, and the summary sons of Gelia daughter of Pharaoh whom Mored took. The apparent two maternal identities are not merged or corrected silently.
column3: How do Adia, Gelia and the unexpressed husband's antecedent relate in the selected text?

column2: Retain the woman Idouia as Nachem's sister, Dalia/Keila, Semeion/Joman and Naem's sons Agarmi and Esthemoe Machathi. The selected longer grouping is not shortened to a familiar parallel genealogy.
column3: How do the initial wife fragment and the subsequent independent father and sons clauses connect?

column2: Retain Semion's Amnon and Rana, Anan's son, and Thilon, plus Isei's Zoath and Zoath's sons. Anan's son is the inherited interpretation of an anarthrous singular son phrase, not an explicitly resolved name division.
column3: Does son of Anan modify Rana, or should son and Anan be divided differently in this name list?

column2: Retain Selom son of Judah, Er/Lecha, Laada/Maresa and families of houses of ephrath abak in relation to Esoba. The borrowed phrase is not converted into a textile trade from another witness without Greek lexical evidence.
column3: What do ephrath abak denote, and how do they attach to the houses and Esoba's house?

column2: Retain Joakim, Chozeba's men, Joash and Saraph dwelling in Moab, the singular he brought them back and abedirin athoukiin. The selected residence is not changed to rule, and the opaque ending is not rendered ancient records by harmonization.
column3: Who is the returning agent, and what is the construction of the final untranslated phrase?

column2: Retain potters in Nataim and Gadera, growing strong with the king in his kingdom and dwelling there. The selected strengthening verb is not reduced to service or occupation alone.
Retain Simeon's Namouel, Jamin, Jarib, Zare and Saul. The inherited forms remain distinct from similarly named figures in Judah's genealogy.
Retain Salem his son, Mabasam his son and Masma his son. The recurring possessive carries successive descent rather than three new immediate sons of Simeon.
Retain Amouel, Saboud, Zakchour and Semei with each son relation. The explicit chain is not collapsed into a bare list.

Retain Semei's sixteen sons and three daughters, their brethren's few sons and the families' smaller increase than Judah. Their remains plural as selected rather than being normalized to his brethren.
column3: What group does their brethren identify, and does the final comparison describe all families collectively rather than each family individually?

column2: Retain Beersheba, Sama, Molada and Esersoual as the first four residence locations. The verb dwelt governs the following continued city lists.
Retain Balaa, Boasom and Thoulad in the continuing settlement list. No alternative town spellings are silently standardized.
Retain Bathouel, Erma and Seklag. These names do not by themselves establish an identification with similar personal names elsewhere.

Retain Baithmarchaboth, half of Sosim, the house of Baroumseorim and the endpoint until King David. Half and house are translated as the selected common words, not fused into reconstructed place names.
Retain Aitam, Enremmon, Thokkan and Aisan with the stated five cities. Four written entries and the number five remain unreconciled; Enremmon is not split into two names without a source decision.
column3: Does the compound-looking Enremmon account for the count, or does another textual explanation apply?

column2: Retain all surrounding farmsteads as far as Baal, their possession and enrollment. Enrollment remains distinct from physical territory and does not imply a modern census format.
Retain Mosobab, Jemoloch and Josia son of Amasia as the beginning of the named-leader list. The patronymic belongs to Josia rather than the entire group.
Retain Joel, the parenthetical this one as Isabia's son, and the succeeding Saraia and Asiel links. The parenthesis exposes the selected interruption without resolving every genealogical attachment.
Retain all seven names from Elioenai through Banaia. The list continues from the preceding named leaders without a new tribal heading.
Retain Zouza's full lineage through Sephei, Allon, Jedia, Samari and Samaios. No intermediate generation is dropped for cadence.

Retain passing through under rulers' names, their generations and multiplication into a multitude within ancestral houses. The inherited wording of the naming/registration clause remains provisional rather than being claimed as a resolved idiom.
column3: Does the selected participle mean listed or enumerated by name here, and how does rulers depend on names?

column2: Retain movement toward Gerara, east of Gai and the search for livestock pasture. Gerara and Gai are not replaced by a different town or a translated valley from another source.
Retain rich good pasture, broad land, peace and quiet and earlier inhabitants from Ham's sons. The explanatory clause does not supply a date or identify every former inhabitant by modern ethnicity.

Retain named arrivals under Hezekiah, striking their houses and the Minaioi, destruction under the ban, settlement and pasture motive. Houses is not changed to tents, and the temporal to this day is preserved despite its compressed relation to the action.
column3: Does to this day describe enduring destruction or the subsequent occupation in this selected clause order?

column2: Retain five hundred men from Simeon's sons to Mount Seir and four sons of Jesi as leaders. The partitive some of them represents the source's from-them construction rather than adding an exact remainder.

Retain striking Amalek's remaining survivors and residence there until this day. The English those who remained condenses the repeated remaining expressions without implying a separately numbered second remnant.
